obligations.definition: Every native metadata field not changed by the specified decode, immediate, branch-mask, poison or cancellation rules is forwarded exactly through both stages, including every declared high bit. Execution output metadata therefore corresponds to issue inputs sampled one edge earlier, while operand data uses current RF input data and one-edge-old zero-source flags. Changes in issue valid do not freeze metadata. One lane's issue contents, source indices or cancellation mask cannot alter the other lane's metadata or operands; shared global kill and branch updates apply by their stated per-lane rules.
obligations.setup: Initialize every native input used by the scenario and establish known legal native-port history before numerical checks; retain unspecified/unreset state according to the contract. Establish two known rising-edge histories; synchronous reset clears execution valid only.
obligations.stimulus: Drive distinct full-width metadata per lane, including nonzero high bits, and propagate through two known rising-edge histories. Change metadata with valid0 and independent lane contents, comparing every unmodified native metadata field rather than only valid outputs. Vary lane source indices, mask/resolve and cancellation histories independently while changing current RF data, exposing lane isolation and distinct metadata/operand histories.
obligations.expected: Every native metadata field not changed by the specified decode, immediate, branch-mask, poison or cancellation rules is forwarded exactly through both stages, including every declared high bit. Execution output metadata therefore corresponds to issue inputs sampled one edge earlier, while operand data uses current RF input data and one-edge-old zero-source flags. Changes in issue valid do not freeze metadata. One lane's issue contents, source indices or cancellation mask cannot alter the other lane's metadata or operands; shared global kill and branch updates apply by their stated per-lane rules.
obligations.sampling: Observe registered values after rising-edge updates against the appropriate pre-edge two-stage input history; sample synchronous reset at the edge. Initialize two known histories before numerical payload checks. Any race-free settled schedule is accepted; no particular clock period, falling-edge driver, fixed delay or observation count is required.
obligations.checker: Predict the specified native outputs from independently maintained input history/state, compare actual versus independently expected values with mismatch failure and nonzero observations. Reference-model equations may be represented equivalently; merely saying model is not full evidence of its unspecified behavior. DUT-derived expected values, permanently disabled guards and always-pass checks are invalid. No fixed observation count or preferred model organization is required.

coverage_policy: Fixed public obligation denominator is unchanged. Stimulus criteria are independent behavioral subdomains, not an indivisible reference campaign: none=0, any proper nonempty subset=1, all=2. Combine actual JSON evidence from multiple tests. Expected prose never supplies absent stimulus. Quantitative reference recipes, clock periods, random counts and model organization are examples rather than behavioral requirements. Complete coverage retains every publicly specified legal boundary. Explicit wrong expected/history, self-oracle and vacuous comparison remain errors with local impact; legal limited coverage is not a wrong behavioral claim.

R-dv-028-001.description: Drive known issue metadata on both lanes over at least two rising-edge histories, then compare registered execution payload and valid timing.
Exercise synchronous reset asserted/deasserted with distinguishable in-flight metadata, valid bubbles and continuing RF-address changes.

R-dv-028-002.description: Drive distinguishable zero and nonzero physical indices and nonzero65-bit RF data through all six read ports.

Vary source type, valid, kill and reset independently of index/data so unconditional addressing and operand capture remain observable.
